    16	
    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	This note fixes terminology for a recurring failure mode in the formalization
    20	of the low individual degree test paper, \path{arXiv:2009.12982}.  It
    21	complements the note-writing policy in \path{docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex} and
    22	the source-statement audit tracked historically in \ghissue{1458}.  The current
    23	source-boundary proof holes are tracked in \ghissue{1507} and \ghissue{422}.
    24	A proof may be blocked at
    25	an intermediate mathematical assertion.  If that assertion is added as a new
    26	hypothesis to a theorem labelled as a paper theorem, the resulting \Lean{}
    27	theorem
    28	may be correct as a conditional statement, but it is no longer the theorem in
    29	the cited source.  The apparent proof has not closed the paper theorem; it has
    30	moved a proof obligation into the theorem statement.
    31	
    32	The protocol below distinguishes such proof debt from legitimate formal
    33	boundary conditions and from genuine mathematical corrections.  It is meant for
    34	contributors and reviewers who must decide whether a bridge, residual, repair,
    35	input, or obligation structure is a proved local construction, a tracked proof
    36	gap, or statement drift which must be repaired before a theorem may be
    37	advertised as a source theorem.  The default rule is restrictive: such data
    38	must not be added to a paper-facing theorem unless it is part of the cited
    39	source statement or a documented faithful encoding of its ambient hypotheses.
    40	
    41	\section{Basic objects}
    42	
    43	\paragraph{Source theorem.}
    44	A source theorem is a theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary in the paper
    45	source under \path{references/ldt-paper/}.  Its hypotheses and conclusion are
    46	the mathematical ground truth, subject only to faithful formal encoding and to
    47	documented paper-gap corrections.
    48	
    49	\paragraph{Paper-facing declaration.}
    50	A \Lean{} declaration is paper-facing when it is named or cited as the
    51	formalization of a source theorem, for instance through a blueprint
    52	\verb|\lean{}| link on a theorem environment carrying a paper label.  Such a
    53	declaration must match the source theorem in its public statement.  In
    54	particular, it may not add an unproved bridge, residual, repair, input,
    55	obligation structure, or other proof-obligation hypothesis which the paper does
    56	not assume.
    57	
    58	\paragraph{Proof obligation.}
    59	A proof obligation is an intermediate assertion needed by the proof of a source
    60	theorem.  It may be a construction, an estimate, a transport lemma, or a
    61	comparison between two formal representations.  If the paper proves or invokes
    62	this assertion, then the formalization should state it as a separate lemma or
    63	theorem and prove it from the upstream hypotheses.
    64	
    65	\paragraph{Obligation discharger.}
    66	An obligation discharger is a theorem or definition which constructs a proof
    67	obligation from the paper hypotheses already available at that point in the
    68	argument.  This is the preferred representation of missing work.  If the proof
    69	is not yet complete, the discharger may temporarily contain a tracked
    70	\verb|sorry|, but the paper-facing theorem should call it rather than assume
    71	its output as an additional theorem hypothesis.
    72	
    73	\paragraph{Conditional helper.}
    74	A conditional helper is a separately named theorem whose statement explicitly
    75	assumes a proof obligation.  Names such as
    76	\leanid{mainFormal\_ofInternalObligations},
    77	\leanid{orthonormalization\_ofInput}, or names whose suffix advertises the
    78	assumed obligation are permitted only when the declaration is not presented as
    79	the source theorem.  A conditional helper is a quarantine for downstream proof
    80	content; it does not close the source theorem.
    81	
    82	\section{Bridge, residual, repair, input, and obligation structures}
    83	
    84	The words \emph{bridge}, \emph{residual}, \emph{repair}, \emph{input}, and
    85	\emph{obligation structure} name possible formal shapes.  They become dangerous
    86	when their mathematical status is unclear or when their names make unproved
    87	data look like acceptable hypotheses of a source theorem.
    88	
    89	\paragraph{Bridge.}
    90	A bridge should be a transport theorem between two already defined
    91	mathematical forms: for example, a tensor-placement identity, a conversion
    92	between two equivalent consistency relations, or a statement translating a
    93	source object into a formal representation.  A bridge is harmless only after it
    94	is proved from previously available assumptions.  It becomes proof debt when it
    95	is assumed because the transport has not yet been proved.  It becomes theorem
    96	drift when the assumed bridge is added to a paper-facing theorem.
    97	
    98	\paragraph{Residual.}
    99	A residual is a named remainder after part of an argument has been performed.
   100	It is often a useful way to record the exact missing target after a completed
   101	construction.  A residual may appear as the conclusion of a helper theorem or
   102	as the input of a quarantined conditional helper.  It is not a permissible new
   103	assumption on a paper theorem unless the paper itself assumes that residual.
   104	
   105	\paragraph{Input.}
   106	An input is a named bundle of data or hypotheses consumed by a construction or
   107	conditional helper.  It is harmless only when each load-bearing field is either
   108	part of the source hypotheses or is produced by an earlier theorem.  It becomes
   109	proof debt when the bundle is merely assumed because the construction of its
   110	fields is missing.  It becomes theorem drift when such a bundle is added to the
   111	public statement of a source theorem.
   112	
   113	\paragraph{Repair.}
   114	A repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or
   115	partial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In
   116	the low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and
   117	orthonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair
   118	should therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the
   119	corresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead
   120	of constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.
   121	
   122	\paragraph{Obligation structure.}
   123	An obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates
   124	needed by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target
   125	or as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement
   126	drift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed
   127	inside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is
   128	proved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing
   129	obligation.
   130	
   131	\section{The main failure mode}
   132	
   133	Suppose the paper proves
   134	\[
   135	  H \Longrightarrow C.
   136	\]
   137	During formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \(B\).  The
   138	paper theorem should be represented as
   139	\[
   140	  H \Longrightarrow B \Longrightarrow C
   141	  \quad\text{inside the proof,}
   142	\]
   143	where \(B\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \(H\).  The following
   144	public statement is a different theorem:
   145	\[
   146	  H \land B \Longrightarrow C.
   147	\]
   148	It is not unsound in \Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the
   149	conclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a
   150	conditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's
   151	conclusion.
   152	
   153	This is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge
   154	hypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted
   155	from the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide
   156	the hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a
   157	paper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a
   158	named internal proof obligation.
   159	
   160	\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}
   161	
   162	Not every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are
   163	faithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include
   164	nonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a
   165	quantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,
   166	or decidability instances required by \Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable
   167	when they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a
   168	condition used implicitly in the paper.
   169	
   170	The distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the
   171	domain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a
   172	mathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis
   173	leaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the
   174	hypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.
   175	
   176	\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}
   177	
   178	Definition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a
   179	definition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,
   180	then every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile
   181	while proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements
   182	can then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because
   183	the wrong definition is still upstream.
   184	
   185	When a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree
   186	protocol.
   187	
   188	\begin{enumerate}
   189	  \item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.
   190	  \item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem
   191	  relating the existing definition to the source object.
   192	  \item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.
   193	  \item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather
   194	  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.
   195	  \item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation
   196	  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.
   197	\end{enumerate}
   198	
   199	This is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local
   200	definition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.
   201	
   202	\section{Allowed shapes}
   203	
   204	\begin{center}
   205	\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\linewidth}p{0.31\linewidth}p{0.32\linewidth}}
   206	\textbf{Shape} & \textbf{Allowed use} & \textbf{Forbidden use} \\
   207	\hline
   208	Paper-facing theorem & Matches the source statement up to faithful encoding &
   209	Carries non-paper bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, or
   210	proof-obligation hypotheses \\
   211	Source-shaped theorem with a tracked \verb|sorry| & Default repair when the
   212	source proof is blocked but the statement is known & Replaced by a strengthened
   213	theorem statement merely to keep the file compiling \\
   214	Conditional helper & Temporary quarantine for substantial proof content whose
   215	remaining named obligation has not yet been discharged & Introduced merely to
   216	avoid a \verb|sorry|, or linked as the source theorem or marked as
   217	proof-complete for that theorem \\
   218	Obligation discharger theorem & Constructs the obligation from paper hypotheses &
   219	Merely restates the obligation as an assumption \\
   220	Input bundle & Collects produced data for a local construction & Is assumed by a
   221	source theorem instead of being produced \\
   222	Obligation structure & Bundles constructed data and estimates & Hides unproved
   223	fields that are then assumed by a source theorem \\
   224	Paper-gap note & Documents a real mathematical or formal-statement divergence &
   225	Justifies silent statement drift without a repair plan
   226	\end{tabular}
   227	\end{center}
   228	
   229	\section{Protocol for a blocked proof}
   230	
   231	When a source-labelled proof is blocked, use the following order.
   232	
   233	\begin{enumerate}
   234	  \item Read the cited source statement and the proof passage in
   235	  \path{references/ldt-paper/}.
   236	  \item Write the paper theorem form, the current \Lean{} theorem form, and the
   237	  first missing intermediate assertion.
   238	  \item Decide whether the missing assertion is a faithful boundary condition,
   239	  a representation adapter, an ordinary lemma from the paper proof, or a real
   240	  paper-gap discrepancy.
   241	  \item If it is an ordinary lemma or adapter, create a named theorem which
   242	  discharges that obligation.  Do not add it to the source theorem as a new
   243	  hypothesis.
   244	  \item Keep the source-labelled theorem itself in the source form, even if its
   245	  proof must contain a tracked \verb|sorry|.  This is the default repair when
   246	  the missing assertion has not yet been proved.
   247	  \item Create a conditional helper only to quarantine substantial proof content
   248	  that already exists and would otherwise be lost.  Do not create such a helper
   249	  merely to avoid a \verb|sorry| or to keep making progress.  If a conditional
   250	  helper remains, give it a conditional name, keep it separate from the
   251	  paper-facing theorem, and record the obligation discharger that must eliminate
   252	  it.
   253	  \item If the source and formal statements genuinely differ, write or update a
   254	  note under \path{docs/paper-gaps/} before marking the statement as aligned.
   255	  \item Update the blueprint so that paper labels point only to paper-facing
   256	  declarations.  Conditional helpers belong in remarks or implementation
   257	  notes, not in the source theorem block.
   258	\end{enumerate}
   259	
   260	\section{Retirement criterion}
   261	
   262	An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
   263	renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all three of the
   264	following conditions hold:
   265	\begin{enumerate}
   266	  \item it is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
   267	        outside result;
   268	  \item no current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated;
   269	  \item it assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data,
   270	        repair data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper
   271	        proof requires.
   272	\end{enumerate}
   273	If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, it
   274	should remain a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.
   275	It should not be a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should
   276	not support a source-labelled blueprint \verb|\leanok| claim.
   277	
   278	\section{Review questions}
   279	
   280	A reviewer should first compare every paper-labelled declaration with the cited
   281	source statement, checking both hypotheses and conclusion up to faithful formal
   282	encoding.  Bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, and
   283	proof-obligation assumptions should be absent from paper-facing theorem
   284	signatures unless they occur in the paper.  If a conditional helper remains,
   285	its name should be explicitly conditional and it should not support a source
   286	theorem \verb|\leanok| claim.
   287	Each load-bearing obligation-structure or input field should have a theorem
   288	discharging it, a tracked issue, or an explicit \verb|sorry| at the obligation
   289	site.  When a definition has changed, the downstream subtree should be checked
   290	against the corrected definition rather than patched locally.  Finally, if the
   291	formal statement genuinely differs from the source statement, a paper-gap note
   292	should explain the mathematical difference and give a plan to remove or justify
   293	it.
   294	
   295	\section{Conclusion}
   296	
   297	The project should prefer visible proof obligations over invisible statement
   298	drift.  A tracked \verb|sorry| in the source-shaped theorem, or in the lowest
   299	named internal obligation needed by its proof, is less misleading than a source
   300	theorem whose assumptions have been strengthened.  Conditional helpers are not a
   301	normal substitute for unfinished proofs; they are temporary quarantines for
   302	substantial proof content, and they must remain conditional until the missing
   303	obligation is discharged.  The paper-facing declaration is reserved for the
   304	theorem proved by the paper, or for a documented corrected version whose
   305	mathematical difference is explicit.

    11	\author{}

    14	\begin{document}
    15	\maketitle
    16	
    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
    20	should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
    21	missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
    22	discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
    23	In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
    24	principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
    25	cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
    26	using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
    27	has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
    28	record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
    29	mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.
    30	
    31	The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
    32	cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
    33	hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
    34	If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
    35	replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
    36	important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
    37	Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
    38	state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
    39	specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
    40	conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
    41	not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
    42	lemma was applied.
    43	
    44	The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
    45	policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
    46	notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
    47	prose.
    48	
    49	\section{Concision and Readability}
    50	
    51	A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
    52	in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
    53	uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
    54	checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
    55	\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
    56	formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
    57	implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
    58	and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.
    59	
    60	The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
    61	\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
    62	reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
    63	source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
    64	and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
    65	derivation genuinely needs room.
    66	
    67	Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
    68	special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
    69	equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
    70	avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
    71	blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
    72	forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
    73	belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.
    74	
    75	If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
    76	stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.
    79	
    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
   107	mathematics.
   108	
   109	Once a cited statement is established to be mathematically false, the repair
   110	and escalation procedure is governed by Section~6 of
   111	\path{local/protocols/issues-prs.md}.  Before asking the human owner to choose a
   112	replacement, a dedicated mathematical-gap session must produce a correction
   113	which is correct, sufficient for every paper and blueprint use, and minimal,
   114	then iterate it against the Lean statement and its downstream consumers.  A
   115	Claude Fable~5.1 session is currently launched by the owner session through its
   116	Agent tool; a Codex main session requests that lane on progress log~\#27 rather
   117	than dispatching a Codex worker.  Only after the astra poller reports
   118	availability on owner inbox~\#26 does the Codex route become
   119	\texttt{dispatch.sh --role mathfix} with astra.  A change to a mathematical
   120	definition or game is escalated immediately; other repairs reach the owner
   121	inbox only after the shared convergence budget expires.
   122	
   123	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   124	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   125	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   126	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   127	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   128	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   129	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   130	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   131	implementation.
   132	
   133	\section{When to Write a Note}
   134	
   135	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   136	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   137	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   138	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   139	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   140	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   141	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   142	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   143	relation.
   144	
   145	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   146	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   147	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   148	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   149	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   150	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   151	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   152	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   153	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   154	
   155	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   156	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   157	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   158	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   159	
   160	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   161	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   162	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   163	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   164	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   165	though it were the paper theorem.
   166	
   167	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   168	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   169	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   170	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   171	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   172	argument.
   173	
   174	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   175	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   176	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   177	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   178	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   179	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the

   361		\begin{equation}\label{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}
   362			V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot \bigl( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \bigr)_{\mathrm{A}''}

   367		\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}

    58	    {I : Type*} (s : Finset I) (B : I → Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
    59	    S.placeSide .bob (∑ i ∈ s, B i) = ∑ i ∈ s, S.placeSide .bob (B i) := by
    60	  classical
    61	  change reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    62	    (heteroKron (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA)) (∑ i ∈ s, B i)) = _

    68	/-- The convolution formula with its second outcome solved for. This is the
    69	third line of the overlap calculation in paper lines 1483--1492. -/
    70	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_eq_sum_sub (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
    71	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    72	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    73	    (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a =
    74	      ∑ b : PauliScalar P, heteroKron ((S.pointMeas side W u).effect b)
    75	        (tauDotProj W (indicatorVec u) (a - b)) := by
    76	  classical
    77	  change S.expPointOp side W u a = _
    78	  rw [S.expPointOp_eq_convolution]
    79	  simp only [Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    80	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    81	  intro b _
    82	  have h (c : PauliScalar P) : b + c = a ↔ c = a - b := by
    83	    rw [eq_sub_iff_add_eq, add_comm]
    84	  simp only [h, Finset.sum_ite_eq', Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
    85	  rfl

    89	/-- The original/pulled-apart overlap is exactly the expanded-point overlap
    90	at the decoded value. This is the first three lines of the proof of Item 1 in
    91	paper lines 1483--1492; it holds for every polynomial outcome. -/
    92	theorem sum_pointMeas_mul_tildeM_eq_decoded_overlap
    93	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
    94	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind)
    95	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    96	    (∑ a : PauliScalar P, S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a) *
    97	      S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a)) =
    98	      ∑ g : Poly P, S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
    99	        S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect
   100	          (dotProduct (decodeFq g) (indicatorVec u))) := by
   101	  classical
   102	  simp only [tildeM, S.placeSide_bob_finset_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
   103	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   104	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   105	  intro g _
   106	  simp only [S.placePlayer_alice_mul_placeSide_bob_tensor]
   107	  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← S.place_finset_sum,
   108	    S.pointMeasExp_effect_eq_sum_sub .alice W u]
   109	  rfl

   111	/-- The pulled-apart consistency defect is one minus the decoded overlap.
   112	This packages completeness with the first three lines of the source's
   113	calculation, still without imposing an encoding restriction. -/
   114	theorem tildeM_consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_decoded_overlap
   115	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
   116	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) :
   117	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   118	      (fun u a => S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a))
   119	      (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a)) S.psiHat =
   120	      1 - avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) (fun u =>
   121	        ∑ g : Poly P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   122	          (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   123	            S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect
   124	              (dotProduct (decodeFq g) (indicatorVec u))))) := by
   125	  classical
   126	  let point := fun u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P =>
   127	    S.placedMeasurement .AA' (leftPlacedMeasurement (S.pointMeas .alice W u))
   128	  let pulled : (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) → Measurement (PauliScalar P)
   129	      (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := fun u =>
   130	    Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   131	      (fun a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a))
   132	      (fun a => by
   133	        apply ProjectiveSetting.reindexOp_nonneg
   134	        exact kronecker_nonneg Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg
   135	          (tildeM_isProj w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a).nonneg)
   136	      (by
   137	        rw [← S.placeSide_bob_finset_sum, sum_tildeM_eq_one]
   138	        change reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   139	          (heteroKron (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   140	            (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB))) = 1
   141	        rw [heteroKron_one_one]
   142	        ext row col
   143	        simp [reindexOp, Matrix.one_apply])
   144	  have h := consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap
   145	    (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) point pulled S.psiHat
   146	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) S.psiHat_norm
   147	  change consistencyDefect _ _ _ S.psiHat = 1 - avgOver _ (fun u =>
   148	    ∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   149	      (S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a) *
   150	        S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a))) at h
   151	  refine h.trans ?_
   152	  congr 1
   153	  apply avgOver_congr
   154	  intro u
   155	  rw [← stateQForm_finset_sum, sum_pointMeas_mul_tildeM_eq_decoded_overlap,
   156	    stateQForm_finset_sum]
   157	
   158	open scoped Classical in
   159	/-- Replacing polynomial evaluation by decoded evaluation loses at most the
   160	mass of the non-encoding outcomes. This is the support-restricted replacement
   161	for the fourth line of paper lines 1483--1492. No mass estimate is assumed. -/
   162	theorem marginal_eval_overlap_le_decoded_add_nonencoding
   163	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
   164	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind)
   165	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   166	    (∑ g : Poly P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   167	      (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   168	        S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1)))) ≤
   169	      (∑ g : Poly P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   170	        (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   171	          S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect
   172	            (dotProduct (decodeFq g) (indicatorVec u))))) +
   173	      ∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g : Poly P => ¬ IsEncoding g),
   174	        stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g)) := by
   175	  classical
   176	  have hpos (g : Poly P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   177	      0 ≤ stateQForm S.psiHat
   178	        (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   179	          S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a)) :=
   180	    stateQForm_nonneg _ (S.place_mul_place_nonneg .BB' .AB'' (by trivial)
   181	      ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).pos g) ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).pos a))
   182	  have hsum (g : Poly P) :
   183	      (∑ a : PauliScalar P, stateQForm S.psiHat
   184	        (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g) *
   185	          S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a))) =
   186	        stateQForm S.psiHat (S.place .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).effect g)) := by
   187	    have hc : (∑ a : PauliScalar P,
   188	        S.place .AB'' ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a)) = 1 :=
   189	      (S.placedMeasurement .AB'' (S.pointMeasExp .alice W u)).sum_eq_one
   190	    rw [← stateQForm_finset_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum, hc, mul_one]
   191	  rw [Finset.sum_filter, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   192	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   193	  intro g _
   194	  by_cases hg : IsEncoding g
   195	  · simp only [hg, not_true_eq_false, if_false, add_zero]
   196	    rw [decodeFq_dotProduct_indicatorVec hg u]
   197	    rfl
   198	  · simp only [hg, not_false_eq_true, if_true]
   199	    have hle := Finset.single_le_sum (fun a _ => hpos g a)
   200	      (Finset.mem_univ (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1))
   201	    rw [hsum] at hle
   202	    exact hle.trans (le_add_of_nonneg_left (hpos g _))
   203	
   204	
   205	
   206	end

    28	/-- For a supplied global polynomial-pair witness, the pulled-apart defect is
    29	bounded by its point-consistency error plus the non-encoding mass. This is the
    30	support-restricted form of the calculation in paper
    31	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1483-1492`, supporting blueprint
    32	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`. It uses no estimate for the non-encoding mass;
    33	the need for that separate estimate is explained in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`. -/
    35	theorem tildeM_consistencyDefect_le_deltaG_add_nonencoding
    36	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
    37	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) :
    38	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
    39	      (fun u a => S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a))
    40	      (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a)) S.psiHat ≤
    41	      deltaG + nonencodingMarginalMass w .bob W := by
    42	  classical
    43	  let mu := uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    44	  let evaluated := fun u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P =>
    45	    S.placedMeasurement .BB' ((w.marginalPoly .bob W).postprocess

     6	/-!
     7	# Polynomial outcomes in the pulling argument
     8	
     9	The joint measurement of a polynomial marginal and an ideal Pauli register
    10	returns the difference between the polynomial and the encoding of the register.
    11	Decoding this difference gives exactly the pulled-apart measurement. Polynomial
    12	collision estimates apply to these representatives without an encoding-support
    13	restriction on the original marginal.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	- Blueprint `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, Item 2.
    18	- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1530-1605`,
    19	  `eq:qld-pulling-11`, `eq:qld-pulling-12`, and the following symmetry argument.
    20	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`; only decoder linearity and its
    21	  left-inverse identity are used here.
    22	- Issue #520; these auxiliary results do not assert `eq:qld-pulling-cons`.
    23	- The imported collision estimate is preserved from PR #539 at
    24	  `ca866da402947c9ee7e1dd5e935a2782fe0d1602`.
    25	-/

    39	/-- The outcome `g - g_h` in `eq:qld-pulling-12` is a bounded polynomial
    40	representative, even when `g` is not in the encoding image. -/
    41	def pullingPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (outcome : Poly P × PauliRegister P) : Poly P :=
    42	  outcome.1 - encodingPoly outcome.2
    43	
    44	/-- Decoder linearity identifies the label in `eq:qld-pulling-12`. This uses
    45	`Dec(g_h) = h`, never the reverse identity on arbitrary polynomials. -/
    46	theorem decodeFq_pullingPoly {P : AdmissibleParams}
    47	    (outcome : Poly P × PauliRegister P) :
    48	    decodeFq (pullingPoly outcome) = decodeFq outcome.1 - outcome.2 := by
    49	  have hsub (g h : Poly P) : decodeFq (g - h) = decodeFq g - decodeFq h := by
    50	    funext y
    51	    simp [decodeOn, decodeAt, evalPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_sub]
    52	  rw [pullingPoly, hsub, decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding]
    53	
    54	/-- Equal difference polynomials give identical scalar labels in the symmetric
    55	expression following `eq:qld-pulling-12`, for every register vector. -/
    56	theorem pulling_label_eq_of_poly_eq {P : AdmissibleParams}
    57	    (first second : Poly P × PauliRegister P)
    58	    (h : pullingPoly first = pullingPoly second) (u : PauliRegister P) :
    59	    dotProduct (decodeFq first.1 - first.2) u =
    60	      dotProduct (decodeFq second.1 - second.2) u := by
    61	  rw [← decodeFq_pullingPoly, ← decodeFq_pullingPoly, h]
    62	
    63	/-- The projective measurement with polynomial outcomes `g - g_h` used to
    64	organize the last step of the pulling argument. Its input witness remains
    65	supplied; no global witness is constructed by this definition. -/
    66	def pullingMeas {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
    67	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
    68	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) :
    69	    Measurement (Poly P) (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
    70	  (tensorMeasurement (w.marginalPoly side W) (pauliRegisterMeas W)).postprocess pullingPoly
    71	
    72	/-- The joint effects are tensor products of orthogonal projections, and
    73	postprocessing retains projectivity. -/
    74	theorem pullingMeas_isProjective {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
    75	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
    76	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) :
    77	    Measurement.IsProjective (pullingMeas w side W) := by
    78	  apply SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective
    79	  intro outcome
    80	  exact MakingMeasurementsProjective.isProj_kronecker
    81	    (w.marginalPoly_isProjective side W outcome.1)
    82	    ⟨by simp [IsIdempotentElem, pauliRegisterMeas, Measurement.ofSumEqOne,
    83	        pauliProj_mul_pauliProj],
    84	      (posSemidef_pauliProj W outcome.2).isHermitian⟩
    85	
    86	/-- Decoding the difference-polynomial measurement recovers `eq:tilde_M`
    87	exactly. The equality holds on the full bounded polynomial carrier. -/
    88	theorem pullingMeas_postprocess_effect {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
    89	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
    90	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
    91	    ((pullingMeas w side W).postprocess (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)).effect a =
    92	      tildeM w side W u a := by
    93	  classical
    94	  rw [pullingMeas, Measurement.postprocess_comp]
    95	  simp only [Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter,
    96	    decodeFq_pullingPoly, tensorMeasurement, Measurement.ofSumEqOne, pauliRegisterMeas]
    97	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    98	  unfold tildeM tauDotProj bracketOp
    99	  simp_rw [heteroKron_finset_sum_right, Finset.sum_filter]
   100	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   101	  intro g _
   102	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   103	  intro h _
   104	  have hlabel : dotProduct (decodeFq g - h) u = a ↔
   105	      dotProduct h u = dotProduct (decodeFq g) u - a := by
   106	    rw [sub_dotProduct]
   107	    constructor <;> intro heq <;> linear_combination -heq
   108	  simp only [hlabel]

   110	/-- The coordinate change to two extraction blocks preserves the consistency
   111	defect, including every off-diagonal outcome and the question distribution. -/
   112	private theorem consistencyDefect_placeSide_eq {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon : ℝ}
   113	    {X A : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A]
   114	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (mu : Distribution X)
   115	    (left : X → A → Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace .alice)))
   116	    (right : X → A → Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace .bob))) :
   117	    consistencyDefect mu (fun x a => S.placeSide .alice (left x a))
   118	        (fun x a => S.placeSide .bob (right x a)) S.psiHat =
   119	      consistencyDefect mu (fun x a => heteroKron (left x a) 1)
   120	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (right x a))
   121	        (reindexState (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) S.psiHat) := by
   122	  unfold consistencyDefect
   123	  apply avgOver_congr
   124	  intro x
   125	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   126	  intro a _
   127	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   128	  intro b _
   129	  by_cases hab : a = b
   130	  · simp only [hab, if_true]
   131	  · simp only [if_neg hab, consistency_term_eq_stateQForm]
   132	    rw [stateQForm_reindexState, reindexOp_mul]
   133	    rfl

   135	/-- Polynomial collision and deterministic decoding, before choosing a
   136	register placement. This separates the finite probability calculation from
   137	the six-register coordinate identities. -/
   138	private theorem polynomial_decoding_defect_le_evaluated_add {P : AdmissibleParams}
   139	    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   140	    (A : Measurement (Poly P) I) (B : Measurement (Poly P) J)
   141	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (hpsi : ‖psi‖ = 1) :
   142	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   143	        (fun u a => heteroKron
   144	          ((A.postprocess (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)).effect a) 1)
   145	        (fun u a => heteroKron 1
   146	          ((B.postprocess (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)).effect a)) psi ≤
   147	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   148	        (fun u a => heteroKron ((A.postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a) 1)
   149	        (fun u a => heteroKron 1 ((B.postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a)) psi +
   150	          (P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q := by
   151	  have hcollision := SandwichProduct.point_codeword_defect_le_avg_evaluated_add
   152	    A B psi evalPoly ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q) hpsi
   153	    (by positivity) (fun g h hne => poly_eval_collision_le g h hne)
   154	  have hpost (u : PauliRegister P) := consistencyDefect_postprocess_le
   155	    (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => A) (fun _ => B) psi
   156	    (fun g => dotProduct (decodeFq g) u)
   157	  simp only [consistencyDefect, avgOver_uniform_const,
   158	    consistency_term_eq_stateQForm, placed_product_stateQForm_eq] at hpost
   159	  simp only [consistencyDefect, consistency_term_eq_stateQForm,
   160	    placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   161	  exact (avgOver_mono _ _ _ hpost).trans
   162	    ((avgOver_uniform_const _).le.trans hcollision)

   164	/-- The last polynomial-collision step of the pulling argument, followed by
   165	decoding. The field-measurement defect is bounded by the evaluated
   166	difference-polynomial defect plus exactly `m * d / q`.
   167	
   168	This is an unconditional comparison of two actual defects for the supplied
   169	measurement. Bounding the evaluated defect from the witness's point
   170	consistency remains the preceding steps of `eq:qld-pulling-cons`; no estimate
   171	for that defect is assumed here. The state and placements are the original

     7	Evaluation of the difference polynomial gives `g(u) - g_h(u)`. Unlike
     8	evaluation after decoding, this formula holds for every polynomial outcome.
     9	The resulting point overlaps are the ones supplied by the global witness.

    17	  modules are preserved from PR #539, head
    18	  `ca866da402947c9ee7e1dd5e935a2782fe0d1602`.
    19	- Issue #520. These identities do not construct the global witness.

    31	/-- Evaluation of the difference measurement is a convolution with the ideal
    32	Pauli point projectors. No encoding hypothesis on `g` is needed. -/
    33	theorem pullingMeas_eval_effect {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
    34	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
    35	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    36	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    37	    ((pullingMeas w side W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a =
    38	      ∑ g : Poly P, heteroKron ((w.marginalPoly side W).effect g)
    39	        (tauDotProj W (indicatorVec u) (evalPoly g u - a)) := by
    40	  rw [pullingMeas, Measurement.postprocess_comp]
    41	  have heval (outcome : Poly P × PauliRegister P) :
    42	      evalPoly (pullingPoly outcome) u =
    43	        evalPoly outcome.1 u - dotProduct outcome.2 (indicatorVec u) := by
    44	    change MvPolynomial.eval u (outcome.1.1 - lowDegreeEncoding outcome.2) = _
    45	    rw [MvPolynomial.eval_sub]
    46	    exact congrArg (evalPoly outcome.1 u - ·) (lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct outcome.2 u)
    47	  simp only [Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter, heval,
    48	    tensorMeasurement, Measurement.ofSumEqOne, pauliRegisterMeas]
    49	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    50	  unfold tauDotProj bracketOp
    51	  simp_rw [heteroKron_finset_sum_right, Finset.sum_filter]
    52	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    53	  intro g _
    54	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    55	  intro h _
    56	  have hlabel : evalPoly g u - dotProduct h (indicatorVec u) = a ↔
    57	      dotProduct h (indicatorVec u) = evalPoly g u - a := by
    58	    constructor <;> intro heq <;> linear_combination -heq
    59	  simp only [hlabel]
    60	
    61	/-- Alice's evaluated difference measurement has precisely the overlap with
    62	Bob's point measurement that appears in the witness's Alice consistency field. -/
    63	theorem sum_pullingMeas_eval_mul_pointMeas {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
    64	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
    65	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    66	    (∑ a : PauliScalar P, S.placeSide .alice
    67	      (((pullingMeas w .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a) *
    68	        S.placePlayer .bob ((S.pointMeas .bob W u).effect a)) =
    69	      ∑ g : Poly P, S.place .AA' ((w.marginalPoly .alice W).effect g) *
    70	        S.place .BA'' ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).effect (evalPoly g u)) := by
    71	  simp only [pullingMeas_eval_effect, S.placeSide_alice_finset_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
    72	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    73	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    74	  intro g _
    75	  simp only [S.placeSide_alice_tensor_mul_placePlayer_bob]
    76	  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← S.place_finset_sum, S.pointMeasExp_effect_eq_sum_sub .bob W u]
    77	  rfl

    79	/-- The reverse-player overlap uses the witness's Bob consistency field, with
    80	the original `BB'` and `AB''` placements retained. -/
    81	theorem sum_pointMeas_mul_pullingMeas_eval {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
    82	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
    83	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    84	    (∑ a : PauliScalar P, S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a) *

    86	        (((pullingMeas w .bob W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a)) =

    91	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    92	  intro g _

    94	  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← S.place_finset_sum, S.pointMeasExp_effect_eq_sum_sub .alice W u]

    26	/-- Place a complete measurement on its three-register extraction block. -/
    27	private def pullingPlacedMeasurement {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon : ℝ}
    28	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (side : PlayerSide) {A : Type*} [Fintype A]
    29	    (M : Measurement A (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side))) :
    30	    Measurement A (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
    31	  refine Measurement.ofSumEqOne (fun a => S.placeSide side (M.effect a)) ?_ ?_
    32	  · intro a
    33	    cases side
    34	    · exact ProjectiveSetting.reindexOp_nonneg _
    35	        (kronecker_nonneg (M.pos a) Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)
    36	    · exact ProjectiveSetting.reindexOp_nonneg _
    37	        (kronecker_nonneg Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg (M.pos a))
    38	  · cases side
    39	    · rw [← S.placeSide_alice_finset_sum, M.sum_eq_one]
    40	      change reindexOp _ (heteroKron (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
    41	        (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB))) = 1
    42	      rw [heteroKron_one_one]
    43	      ext row col
    44	      simp [reindexOp, Matrix.one_apply]
    45	    · rw [← S.placeSide_bob_finset_sum, M.sum_eq_one]
    46	      change reindexOp _ (heteroKron (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
    47	        (1 : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB))) = 1
    48	      rw [heteroKron_one_one]
    49	      ext row col
    50	      simp [reindexOp, Matrix.one_apply]

    80	/-- The Alice evaluation defect is bounded by the supplied global consistency
    81	error, with no decoder correction or non-encoding mass term. -/
    82	theorem pullingMeas_eval_point_consistent_alice {P : AdmissibleParams}
    83	    {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
    84	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) :
    85	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
    86	      (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice
    87	        (((pullingMeas w .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a))
    88	      (fun u a => S.placePlayer .bob ((S.pointMeas .bob W u).effect a)) S.psiHat ≤
    89	        deltaG := by
    90	  let mu := uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    91	  let pulled := fun u => pullingPlacedMeasurement S .alice
    92	    ((pullingMeas w .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u))
    93	  let point := fun u => S.placedMeasurement .BB' (leftPlacedMeasurement (S.pointMeas .bob W u))
    94	  let marginal := fun u => S.placedMeasurement .AA'
    95	    ((w.marginalPoly .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u))
    96	  let expanded := fun u => S.placedMeasurement .BA'' (S.pointMeasExp .bob W u)
    97	  have hp := consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap mu pulled point S.psiHat
    98	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) S.psiHat_norm
    99	  have hm := consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap mu marginal expanded S.psiHat
   100	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) S.psiHat_norm
   101	  have heq : consistencyDefect mu (fun u a => (pulled u).effect a)
   102	      (fun u a => (point u).effect a) S.psiHat =
   103	      consistencyDefect mu (fun u a => (marginal u).effect a)
   104	        (fun u a => (expanded u).effect a) S.psiHat := by
   105	    rw [hp, hm]
   106	    apply congrArg (1 - ·)
   107	    apply avgOver_congr
   108	    intro u
   109	    simp only [pulled, point, marginal, expanded, pullingPlacedMeasurement_effect,
   110	      ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect]
   111	    change (∑ a, stateQForm S.psiHat (S.placeSide .alice
   112	      (((pullingMeas w .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a) *
   113	      S.placePlayer .bob ((S.pointMeas .bob W u).effect a))) = _

   120	  change consistencyDefect mu (fun u a => (marginal u).effect a)
   121	    (fun u a => (expanded u).effect a) S.psiHat ≤ deltaG at hbound
   122	  exact heq.le.trans hbound

   168	/-- Tensoring the strategy state with the two normalized EPR states preserves
   169	the point-measurement consistency defect. This is the six-register form of
   170	the point self-consistency used at `eq:qld-pulling-3`. -/
   171	theorem point_consistencyDefect_psiHat {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon : ℝ}
   172	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (W : PauliKind) :
   173	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   174	        (fun u a => S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a))
   175	        (fun u a => S.placePlayer .bob ((S.pointMeas .bob W u).effect a)) S.psiHat =
   176	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   177	        (fun u a => heteroKron ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a) 1)
   178	        (fun u a => heteroKron 1 ((S.pointMeas .bob W u).effect a)) S.toStrategy.ψ := by
   179	  classical
   180	  have htransfer (A : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) (B : Op S.toStrategy.ιB)
   181	      (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) :
   182	      stateQForm S.psiHat (S.placePlayer .alice A * S.placePlayer .bob B) =
   183	        stateQForm S.toStrategy.ψ (heteroKron A 1 * heteroKron 1 B) := by
   184	    letI : DecidableEq (((S.toStrategy.ιA × S.toStrategy.ιB) ×
   185	        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) :=
   186	      instDecidableEqProd
   187	    have hAB := heteroKron_isHermitian A B hA hB
   188	    rw [placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   189	    change stateQForm S.psiHat
   190	      (S.place .AA' (heteroKron A 1) * S.place .BB' (heteroKron B 1)) = _
   191	    rw [S.psiHat_eq_reindexState, WinImplications.stateQForm_reindexState,
   192	      WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, S.reindexOp_sixRegShuffle_place_AA'_heteroKron,
   193	      S.reindexOp_sixRegShuffle_place_BB'_heteroKron]
   194	    simp only [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.mul_one, heteroKron_one_one]
   195	    rw [stateQForm_vecTensor_heteroKron _ _ _ _
   196	      (heteroKron_isHermitian _ _ hAB Matrix.isHermitian_one) Matrix.isHermitian_one,
   197	      stateQForm_vecTensor_heteroKron _ _ _ _ hAB Matrix.isHermitian_one,
   198	      stateQForm_one_eq_norm_sq, eprState_norm]
   199	    ring
   200	  unfold consistencyDefect
   201	  apply avgOver_congr
   202	  intro u
   203	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   204	  intro a _
   205	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   206	  intro b _
   207	  by_cases hab : a = b
   208	  · simp only [hab, if_true]
   209	  · simp only [if_neg hab, consistency_term_eq_stateQForm]
   210	    exact htransfer _ _
   211	      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).pos a)).isHermitian
   212	      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp ((S.pointMeas .bob W u).pos b)).isHermitian

   214	/-- The evaluated difference-polynomial measurements are self-consistent.
   215	Agreement and two squared-distance triangle inequalities combine the two
   216	opposite-player comparisons with the original point self-consistency.
   217	The error is linear in the supplied witness error, as required before
   218	the collision step `eq:qld-pulling-12`. -/
   219	theorem pullingMeas_eval_consistencyDefect_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
   220	    {epsilon deltaG : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
   221	    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) :
   222	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   223	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice
   224	          (((pullingMeas w .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a))
   225	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob
   226	          (((pullingMeas w .bob W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a))
   227	        S.psiHat ≤ 12 * deltaG + 8 * (Fintype.card PauliEdge : ℝ) * epsilon := by
   228	  let mu := uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   229	  let A := fun u => pullingPlacedMeasurement S .alice
   230	    ((pullingMeas w .alice W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u))
   231	  let B := fun u => pullingPlacedMeasurement S .bob
   232	    ((pullingMeas w .bob W).postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u))
   233	  let PA := fun u => S.placedMeasurement .AA'
   234	    (leftPlacedMeasurement (S.pointMeas .alice W u))
   235	  let PB := fun u => S.placedMeasurement .BB'
   236	    (leftPlacedMeasurement (S.pointMeas .bob W u))

     5	# Finite-character estimates for extracted observables
     6	
     7	Parseval identifies the uniform average over field characters with the sum of
     8	squared outcome norms. A fixed binary basis character instead admits a bound
     9	by four times the consistency defect, using binary postprocessing.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	These are finite-dimensional auxiliary results for blueprint
    14	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, Item 2, and paper
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1542-1551`.
    16	They do not assert the preceding pulled-apart measurement comparison
    17	`eq:qld-pulling-cons`, which remains an obligation of issue #520.
    18	-/

    30	/-- Parseval for the fixed field trace, with a uniform character average and
    31	an unnormalized outcome sum. This specializes the orthogonality theorem used
    32	for blueprint `lem:qld-4-10`; no measurement assumptions are needed. -/
    33	theorem avg_norm_fixed_character_sum_sq {P : AdmissibleParams} {E : Type*}
    34	    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] (v : PauliScalar P → E) :
    35	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P)) (fun r =>
    36	      ‖∑ a, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (r * a)) • v a‖ ^ 2) =
    37	      ∑ a, ‖v a‖ ^ 2 := by
    38	  classical
    39	  have horth (a b : PauliScalar P) :
    40	      ∑ r : PauliScalar P,
    41	        (starRingEnd ℂ) (phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (r * a))) *
    42	          phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (r * b)) =
    43	        if a = b then ((Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℝ) : ℂ) else 0 := by
    44	    simpa only [← Complex.star_def, star_phaseSign, Complex.ofReal_natCast] using
    45	      sum_fixedCharacter_mul_fixedCharacter a b
    46	  rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum,
    47	    sum_norm_sum_smul_sq_of_orthogonal _ _ horth v, ← mul_assoc,
    48	    inv_mul_cancel₀ (Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero), one_mul]
    49	
    50	/-- Multiplication by a chosen basis element only permutes the characters.
    51	The basis coordinate is fixed, not averaged, in this normalized Parseval
    52	identity supporting blueprint `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, Item 2. -/
    53	theorem avg_norm_basis_character_sum_sq {P : AdmissibleParams} {E : Type*}
    54	    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E]
    55	    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) (v : PauliScalar P → E) :
    56	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P)) (fun r =>
    57	      ‖∑ a, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * r * a)) • v a‖ ^ 2) =
    58	      ∑ a, ‖v a‖ ^ 2 := by
    59	  classical
    60	  rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum]
    61	  have hsum := Equiv.sum_comp
    62	    (Equiv.mulLeft₀ (P.model.basis j) (P.model.basis.ne_zero j))
    63	    (fun r => ‖∑ a, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (r * a)) • v a‖ ^ 2)
    64	  change (∑ r, ‖∑ a,
    65	    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * r * a)) • v a‖ ^ 2) = _ at hsum
    66	  rw [hsum]
    67	  exact (avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum _).symm.trans
    68	    (avg_norm_fixed_character_sum_sq v)
    69	
    70	/-- Regroup a field-weighted observable by its binary trace label. This is the
    71	postprocessing at paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1547-1551`. -/
    72	theorem sum_basis_character_effect_eq {P : AdmissibleParams} {ι : Type*}
    73	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Measurement (PauliScalar P) ι)
    74	    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
    75	    (∑ a, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a)) • A.effect a) =
    76	      ∑ b : ZMod 2, phaseSign b •
    77	        (A.postprocess (fun a => fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a))).effect b := by
    78	  classical
    79	  rw [← Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    80	    (g := fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a))
    81	    (t := (Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod 2))) (fun _ _ => Finset.mem_univ _)]
    82	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    83	  intro b _
    84	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.smul_sum]
    85	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    86	  intro a ha
    87	  rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2]
    88	
    89	/-- A fixed basis character costs at most four times the field measurement
    90	consistency defect. The question distribution and basis coordinate are retained
    91	exactly. This proves the final conversion in blueprint
    92	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, without assuming a bound on that defect. -/
    93	theorem basis_character_opDistSq_le_four_consistencyDefect
    94	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {X ιA ιB : Type*}
    95	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    96	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    97	    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement (PauliScalar P) ιA)
    98	    (B : X → Measurement (PauliScalar P) ιB)
    99	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
   100	    opDistSq μ
   101	      (fun x => heteroKron
   102	        (∑ a, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a)) • (A x).effect a) 1)
   103	      (fun x => heteroKron 1
   104	        (∑ a, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a)) • (B x).effect a)) ψ ≤
   105	      4 * consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
   106	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) ψ := by
   107	  classical
   108	  let f := fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a)
   109	  let A' := fun x => (A x).postprocess f
   110	  let B' := fun x => (B x).postprocess f
   111	  have hdef := consistencyDefect_postprocess_le μ A B ψ f
   112	  have hfam := (opFamilyDistSq_le_two_mul_consistencyDefect μ
   113	    (fun x => leftPlacedMeasurement (A' x))
   114	    (fun x => rightPlacedMeasurement (B' x)) ψ).trans
   115	      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hdef (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2))
   116	  have hobs := povm_to_obs_of_measurements μ
   117	    (fun x => leftPlacedMeasurement (A' x))
   118	    (fun x => rightPlacedMeasurement (B' x)) phaseSign norm_phaseSign ψ
   119	  simp only [ZMod.card, Nat.cast_ofNat] at hobs
   120	  have hbound := hobs.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hfam (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2))
   121	  simpa only [sum_basis_character_effect_eq, heteroKron_left_sum_smul,
   122	    heteroKron_right_sum_smul, leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement,
   123	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne, ← mul_assoc, show (2 : ℝ) * 2 = 4 by norm_num]
   124	    using hbound
   125	
   126	/-- The final measurement-to-observable step of blueprint
   127	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, Item 2, on the original six-register state.
   128	The measurement consistency defect is an explicit quantity, not an assumed
   129	bound. Proving its construction-scale bound remains the obligation
   130	`eq:qld-pulling-cons` of issue #520. -/
   131	theorem tildeObs_opDistSq_le_four_consistencyDefect
   132	    {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaG : ℝ}
   133	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
   134	    (W : PauliKind) (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
   135	    opDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   136	      (fun u => S.placeSide .alice (tildeObs w .alice W u j))
   137	      (fun u => S.placeSide .bob (tildeObs w .bob W u j)) S.psiHat ≤
   138	      4 * consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   139	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice (tildeM w .alice W u a))
   140	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W u a)) S.psiHat := by
   141	  classical
   142	  let M (side : PlayerSide) (u : PauliRegister P) :
   143	      Measurement (PauliScalar P) (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
   144	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne (tildeM w side W u)
   145	      (fun a => (tildeM_isProj w side W u a).nonneg) (sum_tildeM_eq_one w side W u)
   146	  let e := sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB
   147	  have h := basis_character_opDistSq_le_four_consistencyDefect
   148	    (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P)) (M .alice) (M .bob)
   149	    (reindexState e S.psiHat) j
   150	  have hd : opDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   151	      (fun u => heteroKron (tildeObs w .alice W u j) 1)
   152	      (fun u => heteroKron 1 (tildeObs w .bob W u j)) (reindexState e S.psiHat) =
   153	      opDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   154	        (fun u => S.placeSide .alice (tildeObs w .alice W u j))
   155	        (fun u => S.placeSide .bob (tildeObs w .bob W u j)) S.psiHat := by
   156	    unfold opDistSq opFamilyDistSq
   157	    simp only [Fintype.sum_unique]
   158	    apply avgOver_congr
   159	    intro u
   160	    rw [norm_applyOperatorToState_reindexState, reindexOp_sub]
   161	    rfl
   162	  have hc : consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   163	      (fun u a => heteroKron (tildeM w .alice W u a) 1)
   164	      (fun u a => heteroKron 1 (tildeM w .bob W u a)) (reindexState e S.psiHat) =
   165	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
   166	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice (tildeM w .alice W u a))
   167	        (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W u a)) S.psiHat := by
   168	    unfold consistencyDefect
   169	    apply avgOver_congr
   170	    intro u
   171	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   172	    intro a _
   173	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   174	    intro b _
   175	    by_cases hab : a = b
   176	    · simp only [hab, if_true]
   177	    · simp only [if_neg hab, consistency_term_eq_stateQForm]
   178	      rw [stateQForm_reindexState, reindexOp_mul]
   179	      rfl
   180	  change opDistSq _ (fun u => heteroKron (tildeObs w .alice W u j) 1)
   181	    (fun u => heteroKron 1 (tildeObs w .bob W u j)) _ ≤
   182	      4 * consistencyDefect _ (fun u a => heteroKron (tildeM w .alice W u a) 1)
   183	        (fun u a => heteroKron 1 (tildeM w .bob W u a)) _ at h
   184	  rwa [hd, hc] at h

    35	/-- For commuting families, reversing the order of the measurements preserves
    36	the consistency defect. This is finite-sum algebra for opposite placements. -/
    37	theorem consistencyDefect_comm_of_commute {X A I : Type*}
    38	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A]
    39	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] (mu : Distribution X)
    40	    (first second : X → A → Op I) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ I)
    41	    (hcomm : ∀ x a b, first x a * second x b = second x b * first x a) :
    42	    consistencyDefect mu first second psi = consistencyDefect mu second first psi := by
    43	  unfold consistencyDefect
    44	  apply avgOver_congr
    45	  intro x
    46	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    47	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    48	  intro b _
    49	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    50	  intro a _
    51	  simp only [hcomm x a b, eq_comm]

    53	/-- A polynomial measurement's mass outside the encoding image is at most
    54	its evaluated inconsistency with an encoding-supported reference, plus `md/q`.
    55	This is the Schwartz-Zippel step in blueprint `eq:qld-nonencoding-mass`.
    56	The reference support is explicit because this auxiliary applies to any POVM;
    57	the concrete reference above proves it without an additional strategy premise. -/
    58	theorem mass_outside_encoding_le_evaluated_defect {P : AdmissibleParams}
    59	    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    60	    (meas : Measurement (Poly P) I) (reference : Measurement (Poly P) J)
    61	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) (hpsi : ‖psi‖ = 1)
    62	    (hsupport : ∀ g, ¬ IsEncoding g → reference.effect g = 0) :
    63	    (∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g : Poly P => ¬ IsEncoding g),
    64	      stateQForm psi (heteroKron (meas.effect g) 1)) ≤
    65	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
    66	        (fun u a => heteroKron ((meas.postprocess (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a) 1)
    67	        (fun u a => heteroKron 1 ((reference.postprocess
    68	          (fun g => evalPoly g u)).effect a)) psi + (P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q := by
    69	  classical
    70	  have hmass := mass_outside_support_le_point_defect meas reference psi
    71	    (Finset.univ.filter IsEncoding) (by simpa using hsupport)
    72	  simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hmass
    73	  have hcollision := SandwichProduct.point_codeword_defect_le_avg_evaluated_add
    74	    meas reference psi evalPoly ((P.m * P.d : ℝ) / P.q) hpsi
    75	    (by positivity) poly_eval_collision_le
    76	  refine hmass.trans (hcollision.trans_eq ?_)
    77	  rw [SandwichProduct.consistencyDefect_placed_eq_avg_point]

import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistanceTheorems.TensorSupport

/-! # Consistency under independent additive convolution

Adding the outcomes of an independently perfectly correlated ancillary measurement
pair preserves the consistency defect. The four register types are independent;
`prodShuffle` places the two registers of each player next to one another.

These are formalization-only auxiliary identities. Perfect ancillary correlation
is a hypothesis of the generic result, to be proved for the Pauli measurements
before applying it to the expanded point construction.

## References

- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-438`,
  the expanded state and the convolution formula for expanded point effects.
- The same paper, `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`.
- Blueprint `def:expanded-state` and `def:expanded-point-measurement`.
- Issue #266; the ideal-point specialization is the separate issue #267.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.Quantum DistanceCalculus

section Factorization

variable {ιA ιB κA κB : Type*}
  [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
  [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]

/-- Joint expectations factor after regrouping an independent pair of bipartite
states by player. The shuffle sends `((i, j), (k, l))` to `((i, k), (j, l))`. -/
theorem inner_prodShuffle_vecTensor_heteroKron
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB))
    (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) (R : Op κA) (T : Op κB) :
    inner ℂ (reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor ψ φ))
        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (heteroKron A R) (heteroKron B T))
          (reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor ψ φ))) =
      inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron A B) ψ) *
        inner ℂ φ (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron R T) φ) := by
  simp only [applyOperatorToState, Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply,
    EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]
  simp_rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [← (prodShuffle : (ιA × ιB) × (κA × κB) ≃ _).sum_comp]
  simp_rw [← (prodShuffle : (ιA × ιB) × (κA × κB) ≃ _).sum_comp]
  change (∑ p : (ιA × ιB) × (κA × κB), ∑ q : (ιA × ιB) × (κA × κB),
    ((A p.1.1 q.1.1 * R p.2.1 q.2.1) * (B p.1.2 q.1.2 * T p.2.2 q.2.2) *
      (ψ q.1 * φ q.2)) * star (ψ p.1 * φ p.2)) =
    ∑ i : ιA × ιB, ∑ j : ιA × ιB, ∑ k : κA × κB, ∑ l : κA × κB,
      ((A i.1 j.1 * B i.2 j.2 * ψ j) * star (ψ i)) *
        ((R k.1 l.1 * T k.2 l.2 * φ l) * star (φ k))
  simp only [Fintype.sum_prod_type (α₁ := ιA × ιB) (α₂ := κA × κB), star_mul]
  conv_lhs =>
    arg 2
    ext i
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  congr! 4 with i j k l
  ring

/-- For positive ancillary effects, the real joint expectation factors on the
shuffled tensor state. No normalization or positivity of `A` and `B` is needed. -/
theorem stateQForm_prodShuffle_vecTensor_heteroKron
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB))
    (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) {R : Op κA} {T : Op κB}
    (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hT : 0 ≤ T) :
    stateQForm (reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor ψ φ))
        (heteroKron (heteroKron A R) (heteroKron B T)) =
      stateQForm ψ (heteroKron A B) * stateQForm φ (heteroKron R T) := by
  have hnonneg := (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
    (kronecker_nonneg hR hT)).dotProduct_mulVec_nonneg φ.ofLp
  have him : (inner ℂ φ (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron R T) φ)).im = 0 := by
    simpa only [applyOperatorToState, Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply,
      EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, dotProduct_comm, heteroKron] using
      (Complex.nonneg_iff.mp hnonneg).2.symm
  simp only [stateQForm, inner_prodShuffle_vecTensor_heteroKron, Complex.mul_re,
    him, mul_zero, sub_zero]

end Factorization

/-- An additive convolution of effect families can be indexed by the ancillary
answer alone. This is the finite-fiber form of the expanded point construction. -/
theorem sum_add_fiber_heteroKron {G ι κ : Type*}
    [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [AddCommGroup G]
    (A : G → Op ι) (R : G → Op κ) (z : G) :
    (∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : G × G => p.1 + p.2 = z),
      heteroKron (A p.1) (R p.2)) =
      ∑ c : G, heteroKron (A (z - c)) (R c) := by
  rw [Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type, Finset.sum_comm]
  simp only [← eq_sub_iff_add_eq, Finset.sum_ite_eq', Finset.mem_univ, if_true]

/-- Averaging a common additive shift preserves the off-diagonal mass of any
weight function. The ancillary joint weights are supported on the diagonal
and have total diagonal mass one. -/
private theorem sum_convolution_off_diagonal_eq {G : Type*}
    [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [AddCommGroup G]
    (p q : G → G → ℝ) (hzero : ∀ c d, c ≠ d → q c d = 0)
    (hdiag : ∑ c : G, q c c = 1) :
    (∑ z : G, ∑ w : G, if z = w then 0 else
      ∑ c : G, ∑ d : G, p (z - c) (w - d) * q c d) =
      ∑ a : G, ∑ b : G, if a = b then 0 else p a b := by
  have hinner (z w c : G) :

        p (z - c) (w - c) * q c c := by
    apply Finset.sum_eq_single c
    · intro d _ hdc

    · simp
